name: Crypto cross-sectional size and momentum factors (C-3 model)

origin.source_title: Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency (NBER w25882; Journal of Finance 2022)

how_it_works.simple: Every week, sort all coins by size and by how much they rose recently. Small coins and recent winners have tended to do better than big coins and recent losers.
how_it_works.analogy: Like picking players for next week's game based on who played well the last two weeks.
how_it_works.precise: Sort coins with market cap above $1 million into quintiles on market cap and on 1 to 4 week past returns, rebalance weekly, and go long quintile 5 and short quintile 1. A three-factor model of crypto market, size (CSMB) and momentum (CMOM) prices nine significant long-short strategies.

rule: Every week, among coins with market cap above $1 million, buy the top quintile by past two-week return and short the bottom quintile (value-weighted); for size, buy the smallest quintile and short the largest. Where shorting is not possible, short BTC instead, as the authors test.
data_needed: Daily prices, market caps and volumes for all listed coins (CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko)
Borrow or perpetual funding costs for short legs
economic_rationale: Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu show crypto returns are not explained by stock factors but by crypto market, size and momentum; momentum is linked to investor attention and size to illiquidity premia.
why_it_might_fail: The size premium lives in tiny coins that are hard or impossible to short and expensive to trade; the paper excludes costs. Momentum works only among larger coins (4.2 vs 0.6 percent per week). Delistings and dead coins create survivorship risk in free data.

reported_results.source: Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu NBER w25882, Table 4
reported_results.market: 1,707 coins with market cap above $1 million
reported_results.notes: Long-short excess returns of 2.7 (1-week), 3.3 (2-week), 4.1 (3-week) and 2.5 (4-week momentum) percent per week; small-minus-big size about 3.4 percent per week. No costs or shorting frictions. Weekly figures of this size compound to implausible annual numbers; treat as statistical evidence, not tradable returns.

reported_results.source: Borri, Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu (2025), Table 2 Panel B
reported_results.notes: Post-2020 two-week momentum long-short 0.021 per week (t = 3.70); size long-short -0.009 (t = -1.69), weaker than the full-sample -0.023 (t = -2.66). Weekly means, not annualized.

post_publication_evidence: Borri et al. (2025) find momentum still significant post-2020 but smaller, and size much weaker (t = -1.69). They cite Fieberg et al. (2024), who test 20,736 research designs and find size and momentum hold across specifications while other crypto factors do not.

implementations.notes: Multi-pair support; cross-sectional ranking requires custom code (for example an informative pairs list).

relevance.reason: Cross-sectional momentum is directly transferable to a basket of currencies, but the crypto size effect is not.
